title: Expansion admission-to-preparation binding
description: Objective: replace the test-only scheduler-to-core expansion projection with one production contract that preserves every admitted authority-relevant byte and can be consumed by the daemon. Deliverable: a focused production bridge/contract between @moe/scheduler admission and @moe/core preparation, plus package tests and the existing integration journey updated to consume it. Resolve the measured gaps explicitly: scheduler admission must carry a verified fairness opportunity reference rather than synthesize one from workItemId; the core admitted shape must bind the scheduler preparation identity and every authority-relevant graph/lineage/capacity/bypass/resource-intent fact exactly once (or document and test a digest projection that makes the same bytes load-bearing); and the hold-to-PlanningRun binding must derive daemon-verified goalVersion from an explicit current authority input rather than an unrelated hand-written constant. NOT in scope: daemon persistence, manual approval handling, child activation, graph supersession, or policy duplication. Hard dependencies: task-2561a780fdd149439c9858c9c7b459e8, task-b863bae80fab426db7b6204f9d713c42, and task-a1e7f75e9681486cb0a8f93e9397b8b5 are DONE. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/core test && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test.
definitionOfDone: A public production bridge accepts only a successful scheduler ExpansionPreparation plus the exact required current authority evidence and returns the closed core ExpansionAdmittedFacts/PlanningExpansionHoldBinding inputs without caller-invented refs or truth upgrades.
Fairness opportunity identity is obtained from validated production fairness evidence and bound exactly once; it is never synthesized from workItemId.

Scheduler preparation identity and every authority-relevant graph epoch/lineage/capacity/bypass/resource-intent byte are either carried into the core binding or covered by one explicitly documented canonical digest, with one-byte perturbation tests proving each production byte changes/refuses the production result.
Hold-to-PlanningRun binding uses the exact reducer-produced hold plus a daemon-current goalVersion input and refuses mismatched hold/current authority with a stable exact code and layer.

The existing integration journey consumes the production bridge and asserts hand-pinned nonzero projection/perturbation case counts; the former test-owned admittedFrom projection and unrelated HOLD_BINDING are removed.
Mutation drills against the production mapping, fairness-ref validation, hold/current-version comparison, and one canonical binding field turn the intended tests red and restore exact bytes.
Fresh pnpm --filter @moe/core test && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test exits 0.
taskRails: Do not solve this by adding a second digest over fields already individually bound; each authority fact must be falsifiable exactly once.
A caller may supply raw evidence for validation but may not declare DAEMON_VERIFIED, invent opportunityRef, or select current goal/hold authority.

Keep dependency direction valid: @moe/core must not import @moe/scheduler. Place the bridge where it can consume both public roots without reversing package dependencies, or expose compatible producer facts from scheduler and consumer readers from core.
Tests assert exact stable reason code and refusing layer; generated sweeps assert an independent hand-written nonzero field universe.
Target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400; explicit owned paths only.

implementationPlan.description: Implement `bindExpansionAdmission` and its full type closure in `packages/scheduler/src/expansion/expansion-preparation.ts`, importing only the public `@moe/core` root. Accept an exact request containing one scheduler `ExpansionPreparation`, one raw fairness opportunity attestation, one reducer-produced hold, and exact current authority `{goalVersion,graphEpoch,holdId,holdVersion,planningRunRef}`. Snapshot every preparation/bound/nested array element through exact own-data readers, recompute `digestOf(bound)` and refuse a mismatched source identity at `EXPANSION_BINDING_PREPARATION_IDENTITY_MISMATCH/PREPARATION`. Validate the opportunity with the production validator and require its winnerWorkItemId to equal the admitted fairness workItemId; pass delegated fairness code/layer through verbatim. Validate the hold outer exact shape as ACTIVE/version 1/terminalReceipt null, safely obtain its creation command, replay it with `reduceExpansionPlanningHold`, and pass through core hold refusals; then require all five current-authority values to match the validated hold and scheduler goal/epoch, distinguishing missing/unverifiable UNKNOWN from proven mismatch. Build and re-inspect a `PlanningExpansionHoldBinding` from the validated hold plus current goalVersion, setting DAEMON_VERIFIED inside the bridge rather than reading it from the caller.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Rejected three unsafe shapes. (1) Do not keep the integration-only `admittedFrom`: QA already proved a test helper is not a production consumer. (2) Do not add `@moe/scheduler` to core or deep-import either package; scheduler already depends on the public `@moe/core` root, so the bridge belongs on the scheduler side. (3) Do not place the full scheduler preparation digest beside every individually mapped field in core admitted facts: that double-binds each fact and lets a dropped mapping hide behind the aggregate digest. The selected design extends the existing scheduler `expansion-preparation.ts` seam: verify the source preparation identity, validate one selected fairness opportunity through the production fairness reader, partition scheduler fields between explicit core fields and one digest containing only scheduler-only fields, validate the active hold by replaying its creation command through the core reducer, and derive the hold contract using daemon-current authority. Existing `.js` bridges remain sufficient, keeping the task to five files.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Measured 2026-08-13 at current HEAD. Design SHA-256 is still `1D9D1EC97D3F07247FBBC088045E0BA2FD6DA8307F10A9026C55106419383191`. All declared producer tasks are DONE in Moe. `@moe/scheduler` already declares `@moe/core`, while core declares only contracts, so scheduler-to-core composition preserves dependency direction. Current production symbols exist: scheduler `admitExpansion` returns `ExpansionPreparation {identity,bound}`; core roots publish `reduceExpansionPlanningHold`, `inspectPlanningExpansionContract`, `ExpansionAdmittedFacts`, `ExpansionPlanningHoldState`, and `PlanningExpansionHoldBinding`. Current reference analysis finds no production admission-to-core caller. `tests/integration/expansion-protocol.test.ts:355-384` alone defines `admittedFrom`, fabricates `opportunity:${workItemId}`, drops graphEpoch/lineage/capacity/bypass/budget-line/resource-effect facts, and the journey separately uses a hand-written HOLD_BINDING. Focused integration baseline is green (1 file, 113 tests), proving the gap is composition rather than existing red. Scheduler plain-Node root currently loads 72 values and `index-surface.test.ts` pins 72; publishing exactly two new functions requires remeasuring and extending that exact namespace guard. Production line counts: fairness-evidence.ts 175, expansion-preparation.ts 208, scheduler index.ts 310; the planned additions fit below 400, with the first remaining within the 250 target and the other two required to stay below 400.
planningNotes.risks: The source preparation and hold are untrusted runtime values despite TypeScript types: snapshot exact own data properties before hashing or reading, reject getters/proxies/custom iterators, and never hash caller-owned values twice. The core `admitted.evidenceDigest` must be a partition digest over scheduler-only fields only: source evidenceDigest, graphEpoch, all lineage fields, fairness disposition/roundsAdvanced, capacity snapshot, provenBypasses, budget lines, and resource effectIntentRefs. Fields already carried explicitly to core (proposal/revision/goal/sequence/children/sources/quality, reservation identities, resource ids/epoch, fairness cap/resource/work item/opportunity) must be excluded from that digest. The separately returned scheduler preparation identity is verified source provenance, not folded into the core digest. Missing/non-data current authority stays UNKNOWN; mismatched current bytes refuse. Validate the supplied hold as exact ACTIVE version 1 by safe outer reads plus replay of its own creation command through `reduceExpansionPlanningHold`; do not accept a terminal hold that the reducer's create replay can reconstruct as active. The daemon consumer task is `task-c4171c1cfe854cb78dd233794b342025`; it must remain sequenced after this task and will own selection of durable current authority.
